parts:
Hi Kasia,

1. Please checkout out arguments viewingwindow and visualreport in the GGIR tutorial, they allow you to generate the pdf report (summary_physical&sleep.PNG)
2. When do.part3.pdf is set to TRUE, the pdfs will be stored in the sub-folder meta/sleep.qc. Note that the timeline for this part3 plot is not very reliable in timezones other than GMT.
3. graphsperday_id_KK_KK_1005-1405.bin.pdf : hashed  are is either your sleep diary or the estimates sleep period time window, blue are all the sustained inactivity bouts that overlap with it and green are all the sustained inactivity bouts that do not overlap with it. If you use more sustained inactivity bout definitions then you will get extra layers added to this.

I have to admit that the visualization in GGIR require more attention both from an aesthetic perspective (nicer colours and visual layout) and from a functional perspective (clearer legends and documentation). So, I would like to call out for anyone willing to dedicate time to, pay for my time, or pay for someone else's time to work on improving this.

Best regards,
Vincent

On Tue, 14 May 2019 at 16:22, Kasia Radziwanowska <koch.ka...@gmx.net> wrote:

Hello,

I am sorry if the following questions are very basic but this is the first time I'm working with GGIR (version 1.9-1) and GENEActiv data.
I was wondering how to receive the same pdf as depicted in the vignette in "4. Inspecting the results" (screenshot in the attachment, "summary_physical&sleep.PNG").
The pdfs I get as output are three files to check data quality, for visualisation of sleep and a file with graphs per day (see in the attachment).
do.part3.pdf and do.visual are set to TRUE, and do.report = c(2,4,5).
However, I get no summary report pdf-file from part 5 as it is mentioned in the vignette in "4.3 output part 5", and no pdf from part 3 - the same three pdf-files are produced when do.part3.pdf is set to FALSE.
Also, I was wondering how to interpret the graphs in "graphsperday_id_KK_KK_1005-1405.bin.pdf", since there is no legend attached. It looks similar to summary_physical&sleep.PNG, so i suppose it is interpreted similarily?

I hope somebody can help me with these questions.

Kind regards,
Kasia
